principles: Correctness and reviewer independence precede token savings.
Every migration decision must be mechanical, versioned, and reversible per role.
Measurements may prove savings or say INCONCLUSIVE, but must never invent equivalence.
drivers: Reuse the trusted full-envelope and fail-closed incremental contracts already shipped.
Reduce repeated reviewer context without deleting role-specific critical lenses.
Preserve old passes and give operators a bounded rollback path during migration.

options.name: A: Per-role modular migration on shared envelope contracts
pros: Small independent blast radius and rollback
Reuses B-dd81/B-03ac facts rather than redefining them

options.name: B: Rewrite all reviewer prompts into one universal template
cons: Creates coupled rollback and authority risk

options.name: C: Keep full legacy prompts and only trim prose
cons: Does not implement trusted conditional assembly

chosen: A: Per-role modular migration on shared envelope contracts
rationale: Choose A because it delivers the canonical Story 5 outcome while keeping each reviewer independently reversible and keeping all safety decisions in existing machine-enforced contracts. B optimizes text at the cost of reviewer separation; C cannot satisfy the full/incremental migration goal.

preMortem.scenario: A modularized role silently loses a seeded critical/high finding lens.
preMortem.trigger: The shared core replaces role-specific instructions or replay corpus lacks the omitted behavior.
preMortem.consequence: Token metrics improve while review quality regresses.
preMortem.mitigation: Preregister seeded findings per role, require detection parity, and return INCONCLUSIVE rather than approve an underpowered replay.

preMortem.scenario: Incremental dispatch is selected after contract, policy, scope, freshness, or authority drift.
preMortem.trigger: A new dispatch path bypasses B-03ac eligibility or trusts a caller-provided flag.
preMortem.consequence: A reviewer sees incomplete evidence and a signed pass may be inadmissibly accepted.
preMortem.mitigation: Centralize selection in the existing policy, add drift/tamper adversarial tests, and bind the assembled envelope to ReviewRun/pass checks.

preMortem.scenario: A rollout failure cannot be isolated to one reviewer role.
preMortem.trigger: One global feature flag controls all five roles or legacy pass reading is removed.
preMortem.consequence: Operators must disable the entire review wave or strand in-flight Stories.
preMortem.mitigation: Use per-role flags, preserve legacy-full-context reads, and test mixed-mode and role-specific rollback.

preMortem.scenario: The 40 percent target drives deletion of necessary instructions.
preMortem.trigger: Budget status is treated as a gate stronger than correctness evidence.
preMortem.consequence: The implementation claims success through smaller prompts despite worse findings.
preMortem.mitigation: Keep budget violation non-blocking for correctness execution, require quality parity first, and record target misses transparently.
